description: The Dragon in the Chinese zodiac: vitality, ambition and confidence, its Earth element, years from 1964 to 2024, and its San He, Liu He and Liu Chong matches.
answer: In Chinese astrology, the Dragon is the fifth animal of the twelve-year cycle, with Earth as its fixed element and Yang polarity. It is traditionally associated with vitality, ambition and confidence. Your animal follows the Lunar New Year of your birth, so early-year birthdays can belong to the previous animal.

sections.heading: The Dragon in Chinese astrology
paragraphs: The Dragon is the fifth animal of the cycle and the only mythical one, which gives it a special place in Chinese culture as a symbol of strength, vitality and imperial power. Its branch, Chen, is linked with late spring, and its fixed element is Earth. People born in Dragon years are often portrayed as confident, ambitious and charismatic, with big ideas and the energy to pursue them. Dragon years are traditionally popular for births in many Chinese communities, reflecting the animal's prestige. Descriptions also mention pride, impatience and high expectations of others. The Dragon is often presented as generous and inspiring when its energy is well directed, and as domineering when it is frustrated or feels underestimated.

Many readers recognise the Dragon in a strong sense of presence and a feeling that ordinary goals are not quite enough. As a Yang animal, its energy is expansive and outward, and it is often at its best when it has an ambitious project to direct.

sections.heading: The Dragon at work
paragraphs: At work, the Dragon is often described as a visionary leader who likes to think big and take charge. Entrepreneurship, politics, management, the arts, law, media and any role with scope for initiative are commonly mentioned. A Dragon tends to inspire confidence, take on ambitious projects and work hard toward goals it believes in. The traditional caution is overreach and impatience: a Dragon may underestimate obstacles, resist advice or lose interest in details. Readings often suggest that people born in Dragon years do best with capable collaborators who handle the fine print, and with a habit of listening to dissent before committing, so that their energy builds something lasting rather than burning brightly and briefly.

A Dragon also tends to perform best when it believes in the mission and has the freedom to lead it. Micromanagement or small, repetitive tasks can frustrate it quickly. Roles with visible impact and room to grow usually keep a Dragon engaged and generous with its energy.

sections.heading: The Dragon in relationships
paragraphs: In relationships, the Dragon is usually described as passionate, generous and loyal, with a strong presence and high ideals about love. A Dragon often wants to impress and protect its partner and to share an exciting life. Its classical allies are its San He partners, the Rat and the Monkey, and its Liu He secret friend, the Rooster, while the Dog sits opposite it in the six clashes. The common relationship friction is pride: a Dragon may dominate decisions or struggle to admit fault. Partners who are confident in their own right, admire the Dragon's energy and can challenge it honestly tend to bring out its warmth and generosity.

Friendships with a Dragon are often lively and loyal, and it tends to be generous with time and support for the people it cares about. It values friends who are honest with it, even when the honesty stings, and it often remembers who stood by it during difficult periods.

sections.heading: Years of the Dragon and their elements
paragraphs: Recent and upcoming years of the Dragon are 1964 (Wood), 1976 (Fire), 1988 (Earth), 2000 (Metal), 2012 (Water) and 2024 (Wood). Each begins at Lunar New Year rather than on January 1, so people born in January or early February need to check the date: in 1964, for example, the Dragon year began on February 13, and anyone born before that is a Water Rabbit. The element attached to each year comes from the ten-year cycle of heavenly stems, so a Wood Dragon and a Fire Dragon share the animal's core character but differ in flavour. Separately, the Dragon always carries Earth as its fixed element and a Yang polarity, which describe the animal itself. Because the five stem elements and twelve animals line up again only every sixty years, the Earth Dragon of 1988 returns in 2048. The Chinese zodiac calculator on this site applies the Lunar New Year table from 1924 to 2044 automatically.

sections.heading: Growth edges for the Dragon
paragraphs: The growth edge for the Dragon usually involves humility and patience. Traditional descriptions mention arrogance, impatience, perfectionism and a tendency to expect others to match its pace. A Dragon may also feel frustrated when reality does not meet its vision. Practices that tend to help include seeking honest feedback, celebrating others' contributions, and learning to enjoy steady progress rather than only big breakthroughs. The Dragon's gift is vitality, the ability to energise people and pursue ambitious goals with confidence. It tends to mature when that confidence includes listening, so that leadership becomes something shared rather than something imposed, and when the Dragon lets itself be ordinary without feeling diminished.

In a Unified Reading, the Dragon often adds a note of confidence and ambition to the wider profile, amplifying a driven Life Path or Sun sign, or giving a quieter one more fire. For anyone born in a Dragon year, these growth notes are prompts for reflection rather than fixed traits.

faq.question: Why is the Dragon special in the Chinese zodiac?
faq.answer: It is the only mythical animal of the twelve and has long symbolised strength, vitality and imperial authority in Chinese culture. Dragon years are traditionally popular for births in many communities.

faq.question: Which animals are traditionally best with the Dragon?
faq.answer: The Rat and the Monkey share the Dragon's San He trine, and the Rooster is its Liu He secret friend. The Dog is its Liu Chong clash and the Rabbit its Liu Hai harm.

faq.question: What years are the Year of the Dragon?
faq.answer: Between 1924 and 2044 the Dragon years are 1928, 1940, 1952, 1964, 1976, 1988, 2000, 2012, 2024 and 2036. Each starts at Lunar New Year, which falls between January 21 and February 20.

faq.question: Which animals are most compatible with the Dragon?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Rat and Monkey share the Dragon's San He trine and the Rooster is its Liu He secret friend. The Dog (Liu Chong) and the Rabbit (Liu Hai) are the pairings readings treat as needing more care.
